children: OTTAWA--Labor productivity for Canadian businesses improved by the most in six years during the second quarter thanks to a rise in the value added in the sector and a dip in hours worked.

Productivity increased 1% in the April-to-June period, the largest rise since the same period in 2020 amid the Covid-19 pandemic, Statistics Canada said Thursday. It marks only the second productivity rise in the last five quarters, after a decline of 0.4% in the first three months of 2026.
Compared with a year earlier, business productivity increased 1.2% following a 0.5% fall the quarter before.
Real gross domestic product of businesses rose 0.9% from the quarter before and 1.9% year-over-year.

Overall, productivity increased in 12 of the 16 main industries tracked by the data agency, driven by a rebound at goods-producers. Mining, oil and gas extraction, wholesale trade and manufacturing were the biggest contributors to productivity growth.

Hours worked in the business sector edged down during the second quarter, after rising 0.4% the period before. Hours worked in goods-producing businesses decreased 0.5% after rising the prior two quarters, and were largely unchanged for services companies.
Canada's economy emerged from the second quarter on solid footing, though risks are elevated as fuel prices remain high and the U.S. introduced fresh tariffs on a range of Canadian goods.
The economy grew at an annualized rate of 3.3% in the latest quarter, the strongest expansion since the start of 2023 and a pickup from modest growth of 0.3% in the first quarter of this year.
On a per capita basis, gross domestic product increased 3.8% at annual rates after advancing 1.3% in the first quarter as the country's population declined for a third straight quarter.
